mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 5.0% consistently precedes positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as it reflects an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations. The mechanism is always active, but the signal direction is positive only when FEDFUNDS is low.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 5.0% in 60% of instances with negative 20-day returns (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 5.0% triggers negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns, as it indicates a tightening cycle that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability. The signal activates when FEDFUNDS crosses 5.0%.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 5.0% in 60% of instances with positive 5-day returns (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE) signal a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day returns. The interaction of these two series is required for the signal.
failure_condition: Correlation between PAYEMS and UNRATE < -0.2 or 60-day returns negative in 70% of instances with expected series movements.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a housing starts rate (HOUST) below 1800 thousand units and a GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.5% per quarter predict positive S&P 500 20-day returns, as sustained consumer demand without overheating supports earnings growth. The mechanism requires both series conditions and late-cycle regime.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1800 and GDPC1 > 2.5% in 60% of instances with negative 20-day returns (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A strong industrial production index (INDPRO > 110) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns, as robust manufacturing activity supports corporate earnings growth. The mechanism is always active.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 110 in 60% of instances with negative 5-day returns (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts rate (HOUST) below 1800 thousand units triggers positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as it indicates healthy consumer demand supporting economic growth. The signal activates when HOUST falls below 1800.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1800 in 60% of instances with negative 20-day returns (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with a declining consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates tightening monetary policy that increases real interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day returns. The interaction of these two series is required for the signal.
failure_condition: Correlation between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL > 0.2 or 60-day returns negative in < 70% of instances with expected series movements.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.0%) consistently predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns, as economic weakness reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence. The mechanism is always active.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0% in 60% of instances with positive 5-day returns (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).
